stimuli.title: नीचे दिए गए गद्यांश को पढ़कर प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।
stimuli.text:
रेत के टीलों के बीच बसे एक छोटे-से गाँव में हर घर के आँगन में एक टाँका बना होता था। बरसात के दिनों में छत और आँगन का पानी नालियों से होकर इसी टाँके में इकट्ठा होता। दादी कहती थीं कि मरुस्थल में पानी सोने से भी कीमती है, इसलिए एक-एक बूँद को सहेजकर रखना चाहिए।

गर्मी की छुट्टियों में शहर से आया मोहित यह सब देखकर हैरान था। उसके शहर में तो नल खोलते ही पानी बहने लगता था, और कोई यह नहीं सोचता था कि वह कहाँ से आता है। गाँव में उसने देखा कि बर्तन धोने का पानी भी फेंका नहीं जाता, बल्कि पौधों में डाल दिया जाता है।

छुट्टियाँ खत्म होने पर जब मोहित शहर लौटा, तो उसने अपने घर में एक नियम बनाया: नहाते समय बाल्टी का प्रयोग होगा, बहते नल का नहीं। उसकी माँ मुस्कुराईं और बोलीं, "लगता है, रेगिस्तान ने तुम्हें बहुत कुछ सिखा दिया।"

stimuli.title: नीचे दिए गए गद्यांश को पढ़कर प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।
stimuli.text:
सर्दियाँ आते ही नानी अपना पुराना संदूक खोलतीं। उसमें घर भर के पुराने कपड़ों की कतरनें रखी होती थीं: पापा की फटी कमीज़, मेरी छोटी हो चुकी फ्रॉक और मामा का रंग उड़ा दुपट्टा। नानी इन कतरनों को जोड़-जोड़कर एक रंग-बिरंगी गुदड़ी सिलती थीं।

एक दिन मैंने पूछा, "नानी, बाज़ार में तो नई रज़ाइयाँ मिलती हैं, फिर आप इतनी मेहनत क्यों करती हैं?" नानी हँसकर बोलीं, "बेटी, नई रज़ाई गरमी देती है, पर यह गुदड़ी यादें भी देती है। इसके हर टुकड़े में किसी अपने की कहानी सिली है।"

उस सर्दी मैंने भी सुई-धागा उठाया। मेरे टाँके टेढ़े-मेढ़े थे, पर नानी ने उन्हें उधेड़ा नहीं। आज भी वह गुदड़ी मेरे बिस्तर पर है, और मेरे टेढ़े टाँके उसमें सबसे प्यारे लगते हैं।

stimuli.title: नीचे दिए गए गद्यांश को पढ़कर प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।
stimuli.text: गाँव में हर साल लगने वाला मेला बच्चों के लिए किसी त्योहार से कम नहीं होता। इस बार सरिता ने तय किया कि वह मेले से खिलौने नहीं, बल्कि कहानियों की एक किताब खरीदेगी। उसकी सहेलियों ने उसका मज़ाक उड़ाया, पर शाम को जब सरिता ने सबको उस किताब से एक मज़ेदार कहानी पढ़कर सुनाई, तो वही सहेलियाँ अगले दिन किताबों की दुकान ढूँढ़ने निकल पड़ीं।

stimuli.title: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.
stimuli.text:
Every Sunday, Mr Bhatia rolled up the shutter of his tiny repair shop near the bus stand and placed a wooden stool outside. It was not for customers. It was for any child who wanted to learn how a bicycle worked.

At first only one boy came, mostly to escape his chores at home. Mr Bhatia handed him a spanner and said nothing about chains or brakes. 'Find out why this wheel wobbles,' he said, and went back to his tea. The boy spun the wheel, frowned, loosened a nut, tightened it again and, after an hour, found a bent spoke.

'You did not need me,' said Mr Bhatia. 'You needed a reason to look closely.'

Word spread. Soon there were six stools, then ten. Parents who had once complained that their children came home with greasy hands began to bring their own bicycles to be checked by the young mechanics, who now argued happily about gears and grease.

stimuli.title: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.
stimuli.text:
Each winter, Tara's grandfather took her to the lake at the edge of their town to count birds. He carried a worn notebook in which he had written the same things for forty years: the date, the weather and the birds he saw.

'Why count them every year?' Tara asked. 'They are the same birds.'

'Are they?' he replied, and opened the notebook. In the early pages there were long lists of names. In the later pages, the lists were shorter. Some birds that had once come in hundreds now came in tens, and a few had stopped coming at all.

Tara was quiet for a long time. That evening she asked her teacher whether the class could start its own notebook. Now, every December, thirty children walk to the lake with pencils and binoculars, and the town council has begun to read what they write.

stimuli.title: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.
stimuli.text: When the power failed on the night before her test, Leela did not panic. She lit the old lantern her mother kept for emergencies, gathered her two younger brothers around it and turned her revision into a quiz. By the time the lights came back, all three knew the names of the planets in order, and the boys were begging for more questions.

questions.stem: According to Erikson, a toddler of about 1 to 3 years who is encouraged to do things alone develops a sense of
questions.explanation: Erikson's second stage is autonomy versus shame and doubt (about 1 to 3 years). Initiative versus guilt follows in the preschool years and industry versus inferiority in the school years.

questions.stem: Skinner developed the idea of operant conditioning mainly from experiments with
options: rats and pigeons in a box
questions.explanation: Skinner's box let rats press levers and pigeons peck keys for food. The bell and dogs are Pavlov, the sticks Kohler and the puzzle box Thorndike.

questions.stem: In Pavlov's experiment, the food that makes a dog salivate without any learning is the
questions.explanation: Food produces salivation naturally, so it is the unconditioned stimulus. The bell starts as a neutral stimulus and becomes the conditioned stimulus after pairing.

questions.stem: Kohler, who studied insight learning in chimpanzees, belonged to which school of psychology?
questions.explanation: Kohler was a Gestalt psychologist: he held that learners grasp the whole pattern of a problem. Behaviourists such as Thorndike and Skinner explained learning through stimulus and response.

questions.stem: A teacher gives a well-behaved child high marks for weak answers because she likes the child. This error is the
questions.explanation: The halo effect is letting one good impression (behaviour, neatness) colour the judgement of something else. Clear marking criteria reduce it.

questions.stem: A child has a mental age of 9 years and a chronological age of 12 years. What is the child's IQ?
questions.explanation: IQ = mental age / chronological age x 100 = 9 / 12 x 100 = 75. Dividing the other way, 12 / 9 x 100, gives the wrong answer 133.

questions.stem: In Maslow's hierarchy, which needs come just above physiological needs?
questions.explanation: The order from the base is physiological, safety, love and belonging, esteem, then self-actualisation. A child who feels unsafe at home or school finds it hard to learn.

questions.stem: Thurstone described intelligence as made up of
options: one general factor and specific factors
questions.explanation: Thurstone's primary mental abilities include verbal meaning, number, space, memory and reasoning. A general factor with specific factors is Spearman, eight intelligences is Gardner and fluid and crystallised is Cattell.

questions.stem: A Class 4 girl speaks well and understands lessons, but her letters are badly formed and her spacing is uneven. She most likely has
questions.explanation: Dysgraphia is a difficulty with writing by hand: forming letters, spacing and writing on the line. Dyslexia affects reading and dyscalculia affects number.

questions.stem: Children in one class learn at different speeds and in different ways. A teacher should
options: seat children by their last marks
give everyone the same worksheet daily
vary her methods and pace for them
teach only to the fastest learners
questions.explanation: Individual differences call for varied methods, materials and pace so every child can learn. One worksheet for all, or teaching to toppers, leaves many children behind.

questions.stem: At the end of a lesson, a teacher asks three quick questions to decide what to reteach tomorrow. This is
questions.explanation: Assessment during teaching that is used to adjust the next lesson is formative. Summative assessment sums up learning at the end of a term or year.

questions.stem: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 applies to children aged
questions.explanation: The RTE Act gives every child from 6 to 14 years the right to free and compulsory elementary education (Classes 1 to 8) in a neighbourhood school.

questions.stem: A teacher asks each child to name two classmates they would like to work with and draws the choices as a chart of arrows. This chart is
questions.explanation: A sociogram maps the choices children make about one another. It shows popular children, mutual pairs and children nobody chose, who may need help to join in.

questions.stem: Studies of identical twins raised in different homes are useful because they help to
options: separate the effects of genes and home
show that twins learn more slowly
questions.explanation: Identical twins share the same genes, so differences between twins raised apart point to the environment, and similarities point to heredity.

questions.stem: Not chosen for the school team, Raju says, 'I never wanted to play anyway.' This defence mechanism is
questions.explanation: Rationalisation gives an acceptable reason to cover a disappointment (sour grapes). Projection would blame others for one's own faults, and regression is going back to childish behaviour.

questions.stem: गाँव के टाँके में पानी कहाँ से इकट्ठा होता था?
options: छत और आँगन के वर्षा जल से
पास की नदी की नहर से
शहर से आए पानी के टैंकरों से
questions.explanation: The passage says rainwater from the roof and courtyard ran through drains into the tanka. No river, well or tanker is mentioned.

questions.stem: दादी ने पानी को सोने से भी कीमती क्यों कहा?
options: गाँव में सोना सस्ता मिलता है
टाँका बनाने में बहुत खर्च होता है
पानी बेचकर सोना खरीदा जाता है
मरुस्थल में पानी बहुत कम मिलता है
questions.explanation: Grandmother links the value of water to living in the desert (मरुस्थल), where every drop is scarce. The other options are not in the passage.

questions.stem: गद्यांश का मुख्य संदेश क्या है?
options: शहर का जीवन गाँव के जीवन से अच्छा है
पानी की हर बूँद का सदुपयोग करें
questions.explanation: The tanka, the reused dish water and Mohit's bucket rule all point to saving water. The passage never compares city and village life as better or worse.

questions.stem: गद्यांश में आए शब्द "हैरान" का अर्थ क्या है?
questions.explanation: हैरान means surprised or amazed, so चकित. Mohit was amazed at how carefully the village used water.

questions.stem: गद्यांश में "मरुस्थल" के लिए किस दूसरे शब्द का प्रयोग हुआ है?
questions.explanation: The mother says रेगिस्तान ने तुम्हें बहुत कुछ सिखा दिया: रेगिस्तान is the other word for मरुस्थल (desert). A टीला is only a sand dune.

questions.stem: "विद्यार्थी" शब्द का सही संधि-विच्छेद क्या है?
questions.explanation: विद्या + अर्थी: आ + अ = आ, so it is दीर्घ स्वर संधि.

questions.stem: "आजन्म" में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation: आजन्म = जन्म से लेकर. The first part आ is an अव्यय (indeclinable) and the whole word works as an adverb, so it is अव्ययीभाव समास.

questions.stem: "लेखक" का स्त्रीलिंग रूप क्या है?
questions.explanation: लेखक becomes लेखिका, as अध्यापक becomes अध्यापिका (अक changes to इका). लेखनी is a pen, not a woman writer.

questions.stem: "पराजय" शब्द में कौन-सा उपसर्ग है?
questions.explanation: पराजय = परा + जय. परा is a Sanskrit उपसर्ग meaning reverse or away, as in पराक्रम and पराधीन.

questions.stem: "काली गाय खेत में चर रही है।" इस वाक्य में विशेषण कौन-सा है?
questions.explanation: काली describes the cow (गाय), so it is a गुणवाचक विशेषण. गाय and खेत are nouns and चर रही है is the verb.

questions.stem: बच्चा अपनी पहली भाषा (मातृभाषा) मुख्य रूप से कैसे सीखता है?
questions.explanation: A first language is acquired naturally by hearing and using it with family and neighbours, long before school teaches reading and writing.

questions.stem: प्राथमिक कक्षाओं में व्याकरण पढ़ाने का सबसे उपयुक्त तरीका क्या है?
questions.explanation: At the primary stage grammar is learned best in context, through stories, conversation and the child's own sentences, not by memorising rules and definitions.

questions.stem: प्रारंभिक कक्षाओं में कहानी सुनाने का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या है?
options: सुनने में रुचि और कल्पना बढ़ाना
परीक्षा के सभी प्रश्न याद करवाना
questions.explanation: Storytelling builds listening, imagination, vocabulary and a love of language. Keeping children quiet or memorising answers misses its purpose.

questions.stem: कक्षा 2 का एक बच्चा अपनी घरेलू बोली के प्रभाव से "पानी" को "पाणी" बोलता है। शिक्षक को क्या करना चाहिए?
options: उसे सबके सामने तुरंत टोककर सुधारें
उसकी घरेलू बोली को गलत बताएँ
बिना टोके सही उच्चारण का आदर्श दें
questions.explanation: The home dialect is a resource, not a fault. The teacher keeps the child talking and models the standard form naturally, so the child picks it up without shame.

questions.stem: कक्षा 4 में वाद-विवाद की गतिविधि मुख्य रूप से किस कौशल को बढ़ाती है?
questions.explanation: A debate asks children to give reasons, listen and reply aloud, so it builds reasoned speaking. Handwriting and spelling are written skills.

questions.stem: Why did Mr Bhatia place a stool outside his shop on Sundays?
options: For children who wanted to learn
For travellers waiting for the bus
questions.explanation: The passage says the stool 'was not for customers. It was for any child who wanted to learn how a bicycle worked.'

questions.stem: Why did the first boy come to the shop?
options: To meet his friends after school
To buy a new spanner cheaply
To get his own bicycle mended
To get away from chores at home
questions.explanation: He came 'mostly to escape his chores at home', not out of an interest in bicycles at first.

questions.stem: What do Mr Bhatia's words 'You needed a reason to look closely' show about his teaching?
options: He wanted the boy to pay him
He thought the boy was careless
He planned to explain it later
He let the boy find the answer
questions.explanation: He gave a problem, not an explanation, and the boy found the bent spoke himself. Mr Bhatia says the boy did not need him, only a reason to look.

questions.stem: Which word or phrase is closest in meaning to 'wobbles' as used in the passage?
questions.explanation: A wheel that wobbles rocks from side to side as it turns, which a bent spoke would cause.

questions.stem: In 'Parents who had once complained ... began to bring their own bicycles', the word 'who' is a
questions.explanation: 'Who' begins a clause that describes 'parents' and stands for them, so it is a relative pronoun. It asks no question here.

questions.stem: Choose the correct word: 'Neither the teacher nor the students ___ ready for the trip.'
questions.explanation: With neither ... nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Students' is plural, so 'were' is correct.

questions.stem: What is the plural of 'ox'?
questions.explanation: 'Ox' has the old irregular plural 'oxen', like 'child' and 'children'.

questions.stem: Choose the correct word: 'Rohit was absent ___ school yesterday because of fever.'
questions.explanation: 'Absent' is followed by 'from': absent from school, absent from work.

questions.stem: Which word is opposite in meaning to 'tame'?
questions.explanation: A tame animal lives with people and is used to them, like a pet goat; its opposite is wild. Gentle is close in meaning to tame.

questions.stem: Choose the correct article: 'Grandpa gave me ___ useful book about birds.'
questions.explanation: 'Useful' begins with the consonant sound 'yoo', so it takes 'a', even though u is a vowel letter. The choice depends on sound, not spelling.

questions.stem: The phonics approach to teaching reading focuses mainly on
questions.explanation: Phonics teaches children which sounds letters and letter groups stand for, so they can decode new words.

questions.stem: In the Total Physical Response method, children
options: write grammar rules in their notebooks
act out commands as they hear them
questions.explanation: TPR, developed by James Asher, links language to movement: 'Stand up', 'Touch your nose'. It suits beginners because they show understanding before speaking.

questions.stem: The direct method of teaching English insists on
options: translating every single lesson into Hindi
questions.explanation: The direct method teaches through the target language itself, using objects, actions and pictures, with no translation.

questions.stem: A main weakness of the grammar-translation method is that it gives
questions.explanation: Grammar-translation centres on rules and translating written text, so learners often know the rules but cannot speak the language.

questions.stem: Shared reading of a big book with a Class 1 class mainly builds
options: print awareness and joy in reading
skill in formal letter and essay writing
questions.explanation: Following the teacher's finger across large print shows that print runs left to right and carries meaning, and the shared story makes reading enjoyable.

questions.stem: What is the place value of 5 in 3,58,072?
questions.explanation: In 3,58,072 the digits are 3 lakhs, 5 ten thousands, 8 thousands, 0 hundreds, 7 tens and 2 ones. So 5 stands for 5 x 10,000 = 50,000. Its face value is 5.

questions.stem: A bangle seller packs 1,184 bangles into boxes of 16. How many boxes does she fill? Type the number only.
questions.explanation: 1,184 / 16 = 74, with nothing left over (16 x 74 = 1,184).

questions.stem: Which of these fractions is the greatest?
questions.explanation: With the common denominator 120: 5/12 = 50/120, 2/5 = 48/120, 3/8 = 45/120 and 1/3 = 40/120. So 5/12 is the greatest.

questions.stem: What is the LCM of 12 and 28?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 28 are 28, 56, 84 ... and 84 is the first that 12 also divides, so the LCM is 84. 4 is the HCF, 40 the sum and 336 the product.

questions.stem: What is the perimeter of a square with sides of 14 cm?
questions.explanation: Perimeter of a square = 4 x side = 4 x 14 = 56 cm. 196 is the area in square centimetres, and 28 adds only two sides.

questions.stem: A bus leaves Ajmer at 9:40 a.m. and the journey takes 2 hours 35 minutes. When does it arrive?
questions.explanation: 9:40 + 2 hours = 11:40. Then 20 minutes takes it to 12:00 and the remaining 15 minutes to 12:15 p.m.

questions.stem: A box holds 200 laddoos. Four children take 38 laddoos each for a class party. How many laddoos are left in the box? Type the number only.
questions.explanation: The children take 4 x 38 = 152 laddoos, so 200 - 152 = 48 are left.

questions.stem: What number does the Roman numeral LXIX stand for?
questions.explanation: LX = 50 + 10 = 60 and IX = 10 - 1 = 9, so LXIX = 69. Reading IX as 11 gives 71.

questions.stem: How many grams are there in 5 kg 80 g?
questions.explanation: 1 kg = 1,000 g, so 5 kg 80 g = 5,000 + 80 = 5,080 g. Writing 80 g as 800 or 8 gives the wrong choices.

questions.stem: How many vertices (corners) does a triangular prism have?
questions.explanation: Each triangular end has 3 corners, so 3 + 3 = 6 vertices. A triangular prism has 5 faces and 9 edges.

questions.stem: A geoboard with rubber bands is most useful in a primary class for
questions.explanation: Children stretch bands over pegs to make and change shapes, count squares inside for area and pegs along the edge for perimeter.

questions.stem: Which is the best first activity for introducing money in Class 2?
options: Playing shop with toy coins and notes
Learning a table of coin values
Writing amounts in words and figures
questions.explanation: A play shop lets children handle, count and exchange money in a real-looking situation before they meet written sums.

questions.stem: A child recites numbers to 20 but, when counting objects, skips some and counts others twice. She needs help with
questions.explanation: Correct counting pairs exactly one number word with each object. Reciting the sequence is not the same as counting a set.

questions.stem: Before formal work on numbers, Class 1 children should mainly be given tasks of
options: memorising tables up to ten by heart
questions.explanation: Classification, one-to-one matching and seriation are the pre-number ideas on which counting and number sense are built.

questions.stem: Which task encourages open-ended thinking in a Class 4 mathematics lesson?
options: Copy the sum from the blackboard
questions.explanation: An open task has many correct answers (3 x 8, 30 - 6, 12 + 12...) and invites children to reason and compare methods. The others have one fixed answer.

questions.stem: Which is the state flower of Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: The rohida, a desert tree with orange and yellow flowers, is Rajasthan's state flower. The lotus is India's national flower.

questions.stem: Tal Chhapar Wildlife Sanctuary in Churu district, on the edge of the Thar, is best known for its herds of
questions.explanation: Tal Chhapar's open grassland is home to about a thousand blackbuck, and it draws migratory birds such as harriers. Tigers live in Ranthambore and Sariska; Rajasthan has no wild elephants or rhinos.

questions.stem: In 1730 at Khejarli, Amrita Devi Bishnoi and hundreds of villagers gave their lives to protect
questions.explanation: The Bishnois hugged the khejri trees that were to be cut for a king's lime kiln. The event is remembered as an early movement to save trees.

questions.stem: The festival of Teej, celebrated with swings and green clothes, welcomes
questions.explanation: Teej falls in the month of Shravan, at the start of the rains, and women celebrate it with swings, songs and fasting.

questions.stem: Desert trees such as khejri have very long roots mainly to
questions.explanation: In dry land the water table is deep, so long tap roots let desert trees reach moisture far below the surface.

questions.stem: A camel can walk easily on soft sand because it has
questions.explanation: Wide padded feet spread its weight so it does not sink. The eyelashes keep out blowing sand and the hump stores fat.

questions.stem: Bajra is a main crop of western Rajasthan mainly because it
questions.explanation: Bajra (pearl millet) tolerates heat, sandy soil and low rainfall, so it suits the desert. Rice, by contrast, needs flooded fields.

questions.stem: Which of these animals is a reptile?
questions.explanation: Lizards have dry scaly skin and lay eggs on land, like snakes and crocodiles. A frog is an amphibian, a bat a mammal and a pigeon a bird.

questions.stem: Rajasthan shares an international border with which country?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan's western districts border Pakistan. Nepal borders Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, and Bangladesh borders West Bengal and the north-east.

questions.stem: Which of these is a fossil fuel?
questions.explanation: Petroleum formed underground over millions of years from the remains of tiny sea organisms, so it is a fossil fuel. Firewood and dung cakes come from living things today.

questions.stem: In the project method of teaching EVS, children
options: investigate a real question over time
memorise facts for a weekly test
answer questions at the end of a lesson
questions.explanation: A project is an extended task: children plan, collect information, record it and share what they found, for example a study of water use at home.

questions.stem: A Class 5 teacher asks children to interview a grandparent about games played long ago. This mainly helps them
options: learn the rules of new games
see how life has changed over time
questions.explanation: Talking to elders brings history into the child's own family and shows change over time, a key EVS idea.

questions.stem: Children collect fallen leaves of different shapes and sort them in a scrapbook. This mainly builds
questions.explanation: Looking closely and grouping by shape, edge or vein pattern are the EVS skills of observation and classification.

questions.stem: A teacher invites a local farmer to talk about crops and seasons. This is an example of
options: a test of the farmer's knowledge
questions.explanation: People in the community are a rich resource. Their experience links the lesson to the children's own world.

questions.stem: Children draw their family and talk about who does which work at home. This mainly helps the teacher learn
options: how many words they can spell
how they see roles in the family
questions.explanation: Drawings and talk reveal children's ideas, including ideas about who does what at home, which the teacher can then discuss.

questions.stem: When her mother steps out of the room, a nine-month-old crawls to the door to look for her. Piaget would say the baby now has
questions.explanation: The baby knows her mother still exists when out of sight, which is object permanence, the key achievement of the sensorimotor stage (birth to about 2 years).

questions.stem: A five-year-old says the wind is alive because it moves the trees. Piaget called this belief
questions.explanation: Animism, giving life and feelings to non-living things, is typical of the preoperational stage. Centration is focusing on one feature of a problem at a time.

questions.stem: A boy who snatches classmates' crayons is not allowed on the swing that day, and he snatches less afterwards. Losing the swing is
questions.explanation: Taking away something pleasant (swing time) to reduce a behaviour is (negative) punishment. Negative reinforcement removes something unpleasant to increase a behaviour, which is the usual confusion.

questions.stem: After her baby brother is born, a six-year-old starts sucking her thumb again. This defence mechanism is
questions.explanation: Going back to the behaviour of an earlier age under stress is regression. Sublimation turns an urge into an acceptable activity, such as anger into sport.

questions.stem: A child who understands her own feelings and strengths well shows which of Gardner's intelligences?
questions.explanation: Intrapersonal intelligence is knowing oneself. Interpersonal intelligence is understanding other people, which is often confused with it.

questions.stem: Guilford's Structure of Intellect model classifies intellectual abilities along which three dimensions?
questions.explanation: Guilford described every ability as an operation (such as divergent or convergent production) applied to a content to give a product. Fluid and crystallised are Cattell's terms and analytical, creative and practical are Sternberg's.

questions.stem: In Kohlberg's theory, a person who follows universal principles of justice even against a law is at the
questions.explanation: At the post-conventional level, morality rests on principles such as justice and rights. At the conventional level, people follow rules and laws to keep order and approval.

questions.stem: Children remember the colours of the rainbow in order through the made-up word VIBGYOR. Such a memory aid is called a
questions.explanation: A mnemonic links new material to an easy pattern, such as a word built from first letters, so it can be recalled in order. It works best alongside understanding, not in place of it.

questions.stem: Revising in short sessions spread over several days, rather than in one long session, is called
questions.explanation: Spaced or distributed practice gives better long-term memory than massed practice (cramming), because each session refreshes memory before it fades.

questions.stem: Judd's theory says that learning transfers to new situations mainly through
options: training the mind like a muscle
questions.explanation: Judd's generalisation theory: a principle understood in one setting can be applied in another. Identical elements is Thorndike's theory and training the mind like a muscle is formal discipline.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to know how each child feels about mathematics. The most suitable tool is
questions.explanation: An attitude scale asks how strongly a child agrees with statements such as 'I enjoy maths', so it measures feelings. An achievement test measures what has been learned.

questions.stem: Which approach helps a slow learner most in a regular class?
options: Giving the child no homework at all
Moving the child to a lower class
questions.explanation: Slow learners need more time, smaller steps, concrete materials and frequent revision. Comparison and demotion damage confidence without helping learning.

questions.stem: At the time of admission, the RTE Act, 2009 forbids schools from
options: asking the child's name and age
screening the child or the parents
giving the child a school uniform
questions.explanation: Section 13 bans any screening procedure for admission and any capitation fee. Recording a child's details is ordinary admission work.

questions.stem: A teacher believes some children are bright, and they do better because she expects more of them. This is the
questions.explanation: When a teacher's expectations shape how she treats children, and so how they perform, it is the Pygmalion (or Rosenthal) effect. It is a reason to expect a lot of every child.

questions.stem: Carl Jung divided personality into which two types?
questions.explanation: Jung described introverts, turned towards their inner world, and extroverts, turned towards people and activity. Id and superego are Freud's terms; endomorph and ectomorph are Sheldon's body types.

questions.stem: नानी गुदड़ी किससे सिलती थीं?
options: बाज़ार से लाए नए कपड़े से
questions.explanation: The passage says Nani stitched the quilt from scraps (कतरनें) of the family's old clothes: a torn shirt, an outgrown frock and a faded dupatta.

questions.stem: नानी के अनुसार गुदड़ी नई रज़ाई से किस बात में अलग है?
options: वह बाज़ार में अधिक बिकती है
वह रज़ाई से ज़्यादा गरम होती है
वह गरमी के साथ यादें भी देती है
वह बहुत जल्दी सिल जाती है
questions.explanation: Nani says a new quilt gives warmth, but the गुदड़ी also gives memories, because every piece holds the story of someone dear.

questions.stem: नानी ने बच्ची के टेढ़े-मेढ़े टाँके क्यों नहीं उधेड़े?
options: उनके पास समय नहीं बचा था
वे उसके प्रयास का आदर करती थीं
धागा पूरा खत्म हो गया था
questions.explanation: Nani kept the uneven stitches because they were the child's own effort; the narrator says they now look the dearest of all.

questions.stem: गद्यांश में आए शब्द "कतरन" का अर्थ क्या है?
options: कपड़े का कटा हुआ छोटा टुकड़ा
questions.explanation: कतरन is a small cut piece of cloth left over or cut from old clothes. The संदूक is the trunk they were kept in.

questions.stem: "नानी हँसकर बोलीं" में "हँसकर" शब्द क्या है?
questions.explanation: हँस + कर shows an action completed before the main verb बोलीं, so हँसकर is a पूर्वकालिक क्रिया (conjunctive participle).

questions.stem: "नयन" शब्द का सही संधि-विच्छेद क्या है?
questions.explanation: ने + अन: ए + अ = अय, which is अयादि संधि, as in शयन (शे + अन).

questions.stem: "रसोईघर" में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation: रसोईघर = रसोई के लिए घर. The case sign के लिए is dropped and the second word is the main one, so it is (संप्रदान) तत्पुरुष.

questions.stem: "सम्मान" का विलोम शब्द क्या है?
questions.explanation: The opposite of सम्मान (respect) is अपमान (insult). आदर, गौरव and प्रतिष्ठा are close in meaning to सम्मान, so they are synonyms, not opposites.

questions.stem: "समुद्र" का पर्यायवाची शब्द कौन-सा है?
questions.explanation: सागर, जलधि and रत्नाकर mean sea. सरिता is a river, and सरोवर and तड़ाग are lakes or ponds.

questions.stem: "सीता घर में है।" इस वाक्य में "घर में" कौन-सा कारक है?
questions.explanation: में and पर show the place where something is, which is अधिकरण कारक. अपादान (से) shows separation.

questions.stem: एक बच्चा "कमल" शब्द को "क-म-ल" ध्वनियों में तोड़कर बोल पाता है। यह किस कौशल का संकेत है?
questions.explanation: Hearing and separating the sounds inside a word is phonological awareness, a key early step towards reading and spelling.

questions.stem: पूरे वाक्य से शुरू करके फिर शब्दों और वर्णों तक पहुँचने वाली पठन-विधि कौन-सी है?
questions.explanation: The sentence method starts from a meaningful whole sentence and then breaks it into words and letters. The letter (वर्ण) method goes the other way, from the alphabet up.

questions.stem: बच्चे से पढ़ी हुई कहानी अपने शब्दों में दोबारा सुनाने को कहना मुख्य रूप से किसका आकलन है?
questions.explanation: Retelling shows whether the child understood the story and can keep events in order. It says little about handwriting, spelling or speed.

questions.stem: निदानात्मक परीक्षण से बच्चे की कठिनाई पता चलने के बाद अगला कदम क्या होना चाहिए?
questions.explanation: Diagnosis finds the specific difficulty; remedial teaching then works on it. A test with no follow-up teaching does not help the child.

questions.stem: मौन वाचन का मुख्य लाभ क्या है?
options: अर्थ ग्रहण और पढ़ने की गति बढ़ती है
उच्चारण की गलतियाँ तुरंत पकड़ी जाती हैं
कक्षा में अनुशासन बना रहता है
questions.explanation: Silent reading focuses attention on meaning and lets readers move faster. Pronunciation and voice are practised through reading aloud.

questions.stem: What did Tara's grandfather write in his notebook?
options: The date, the weather and the birds
The prices of fish caught in the lake
The names of his old friends
questions.explanation: The passage says that for forty years he wrote 'the date, the weather and the birds he saw'.

questions.stem: What did the later pages of the notebook show, compared with the early ones?
options: Fewer birds come now than before
The lake has grown much larger now
More kinds of birds come now
questions.explanation: The later lists were shorter: birds that came in hundreds now came in tens, and some stopped coming.

questions.stem: Why was Tara 'quiet for a long time'?
options: She was angry with her grandfather
She was thinking about the lost birds
She was tired after the long walk
She could not read his old handwriting
questions.explanation: She had just learned from the notebook that the birds were disappearing, and that evening she acted on it by starting a class notebook.

questions.stem: Which word does the passage use for the lists in the early pages, in contrast to the 'shorter' lists later?
questions.explanation: The passage contrasts 'long lists of names' in the early pages with shorter lists later. 'Early' describes the pages, not the lists.

questions.stem: In 'the town council has begun to read what they write', the verb 'has begun' is in the
questions.explanation: Has or have plus the past participle (begun) forms the present perfect. The past perfect would be 'had begun'.

questions.stem: Choose the passive form of 'Asha painted the gate.'
options: The gate was being painted by Asha.
The gate was painted by Asha.
The gate is painted by Asha.
The gate has been painted by Asha.
questions.explanation: The active sentence is in the simple past, so the passive uses was plus the past participle: was painted.

questions.stem: Choose the indirect form of: He said, 'I can swim.'
options: He said that I could swim.
He said that he could have swum.
He said that he could swim.
He said that he can swim.
questions.explanation: With a reporting verb in the past, 'I' becomes 'he' and 'can' moves back to 'could'.

questions.stem: Which word is closest in meaning to 'scarce'?
questions.explanation: Scarce means in short supply, so rare. Plenty is its opposite, and a scarce thing may become costly, but that is not the meaning.

questions.stem: Choose the correct collective noun: 'a ___ of bees'
questions.explanation: Bees move in a swarm. A herd is used for cattle, a pack for wolves and a flock for sheep or birds.

questions.stem: Choose the correct word: 'This is the ___ of the two bags.'
questions.explanation: When only two things are compared, the comparative 'heavier' is used, even with 'the'. The superlative is for three or more.

questions.stem: Reading a short text closely in class for detail, vocabulary and structure is called
questions.explanation: Intensive reading studies a short text in depth. Extensive reading means reading many easy texts for pleasure; skimming and scanning are fast-reading strategies.

questions.stem: Which is a good pre-reading activity for a story?
options: Answering the questions at the end
Guessing the story from its title
Writing a summary of the story
questions.explanation: Predicting from the title and pictures activates what children already know and gives them a purpose for reading.

questions.stem: Giving children a short checklist to review their own writing before handing it in mainly builds
options: speed in copying from the board
the habit of revising their work
questions.explanation: A self-review checklist (capital letters, full stops, does it make sense?) teaches children to read and improve their own drafts.

questions.stem: 'Language across the curriculum' means that
options: English is taught in every period
grammar is tested in every subject
questions.explanation: Children learn language while learning maths, EVS and other subjects, so every teacher shares responsibility for reading, writing and talk.

questions.stem: Krashen's input hypothesis says children acquire a language best from input that is
options: understood and a little above their level
always corrected at every single error made
questions.explanation: Comprehensible input (often written i + 1) is language the learner can understand that stretches them slightly beyond their current level.

questions.stem: Which number is 'ninety thousand and seven'?
questions.explanation: Ninety thousand is 90,000; adding seven gives 90,007. 90,070 would be ninety thousand and seventy.

questions.stem: A school library gets 35 new books every week. After how many weeks will it have received 1,015 new books? Type the number only.
What is 3.6 + 0.85?
questions.explanation: Line up the decimal points: 3.60 + 0.85 = 4.45. Adding without lining up the points gives answers such as 1.21 or 3.69.

questions.stem: What is the average of 18, 24 and 33?
questions.explanation: Sum = 18 + 24 + 33 = 75; average = 75 / 3 = 25. 75 is only the sum, and dividing it by 2 gives 37.5.

questions.stem: A rectangular room is 9 m long and 7 m wide. What is its floor area in square metres?
questions.explanation: Area = length x width = 9 x 7 = 63 square metres. 32 is the perimeter in metres (2 x (9 + 7)).

questions.stem: What comes next: 11, 22, 44, 88, ...?
questions.explanation: Each number is double the one before it, so after 88 comes 176. Adding 11 each time (99) does not fit 22 to 44.

questions.stem: What is 3/5 of 85?
questions.explanation: 1/5 of 85 = 17, so 3/5 = 3 x 17 = 51. 17 is only one fifth and 68 is four fifths.

questions.stem: How many minutes are there in 1 3/4 hours?
questions.explanation: 1 hour = 60 minutes and 3/4 hour = 45 minutes, so 105 minutes. Treating 1 3/4 hours as 1.75 and moving the point gives 175.

questions.stem: Which capital letter has a vertical line of symmetry?
questions.explanation: A vertical line through the middle of A gives two mirror halves. F, G and J have no line of symmetry.

questions.stem: In a class survey, 12 children like mango best, 9 like guava and 15 like banana. How many more children like banana than guava?
questions.explanation: Banana 15 - guava 9 = 6. 3 is the difference between mango and guava, 24 is banana plus guava and 36 is the whole class.

questions.stem: A clock face with movable hands is most useful for teaching children to
questions.explanation: Children set the hands to times they hear and read times the teacher sets, which builds the link between the dial and the time.

questions.stem: A number line drawn on the floor is especially useful for showing
options: the names of solid and flat shapes
questions.explanation: Children walk or jump forward to add and backward to subtract, which makes the operations visible.

questions.stem: A child writes 3/4 + 1/4 = 4/8. What is the most helpful next step?
options: Make her copy the correct rule five times
Give her ten more such sums
Mark it wrong and move on
questions.explanation: She has added numerators and denominators. Fraction strips let her see that three quarters and one quarter make four quarters, one whole.

questions.stem: A child writes 6 x 0 = 6. Which approach best corrects the idea?
options: Tell her the zero rule again
Show six groups with nothing in each
Ask her to learn the table of zero aloud
Skip zero until a later class
questions.explanation: Multiplication as equal groups makes it clear: six empty plates hold nothing, so 6 x 0 = 0. Telling the rule again does not change the idea behind the error.

questions.stem: Regular mental mathematics in class mainly develops
options: fast copying of sums from the board
questions.explanation: Working in the head builds a feel for numbers, flexible strategies and estimation, which also help children check written answers.

questions.stem: In which folk dance of Rajasthan does a dancer balance several pots on the head, sometimes while standing on a brass plate?
questions.explanation: Bhavai is a dance of balance with a tower of pots on the head. Kachhi Ghodi uses dummy horses and Gair is danced by men with sticks.

questions.stem: Leheriya and bandhej are two famous kinds of
options: carving on wooden doors and windows
questions.explanation: In bandhej small bits of cloth are tied before dyeing; in leheriya the cloth is rolled and tied to give wave-like stripes.

questions.stem: The Chakri dance of the Hadoti region (Kota, Bundi and Baran) gets its name because the women dancers
options: spin round and round like a wheel
strike cymbals tied to their bodies
questions.explanation: Chakri comes from chakkar, a circle: women of the Kanjar community spin very fast at weddings and fairs. Balancing pots is Bhavai, dummy horses are Kachhi Ghodi, and cymbals tied to the body are Terah Taali.

questions.stem: Ana Sagar, a lake made by damming a stream about 900 years ago, is in which city?
questions.explanation: Ana Sagar in Ajmer was built in the 12th century by the Chauhan ruler Arnoraja (Anaji). Udaipur is known for Pichola and Fateh Sagar, and Jaisalmer for Gadisar.

questions.stem: Fish take in oxygen dissolved in water through their
questions.explanation: Gills take oxygen from the water passing over them. Fins help fish swim and steer.

questions.stem: Which teeth are used mainly for tearing food?
questions.explanation: Pointed canines tear food. Incisors at the front cut and bite, and molars at the back grind and chew.

questions.stem: A johad, used in villages of Rajasthan, is
options: a covered tank for each home
an earthen dam that holds rainwater
a deep well worked by a pair of camels
a pipe that brings canal water
questions.explanation: A johad is a crescent-shaped mud bank that stops rainwater so it soaks into the ground and recharges wells. A tanka is the covered tank.

questions.stem: Houses in the desert have thick mud walls mainly because they
options: stay cool by day and warm by night
are cheaper to paint every year
stop floodwater from coming into rooms
questions.explanation: Thick mud walls take a long time to heat up and cool down, which evens out the desert's very hot days and cold nights.

questions.stem: Your father's sister is your
questions.explanation: A father's sister is bua. A mother's sister is mausi, a mother's brother's wife is mami and a father's younger brother's wife is chachi.

questions.stem: Which part of the potato plant do we eat?
questions.explanation: A potato is a tuber, a swollen underground stem: it has eyes (buds) from which new shoots grow. A carrot, by contrast, is a root.

questions.stem: An inquiry-based EVS lesson usually begins with
options: a question children want to answer
a test on the previous lesson
a list of facts for children to memorise
questions.explanation: Inquiry starts from children's curiosity: 'Why do leaves fall?' They then observe, test and discuss to answer it.

questions.stem: On a nature walk, a teacher notes whether each child observes closely and records details. She is assessing
options: speed of reading the textbook aloud
questions.explanation: Observing and recording are EVS process skills, best assessed by watching children at work with a checklist.

questions.stem: A child asks why the moon changes shape, and the teacher is not sure. She should
options: say it is not in the syllabus
ask the child to stop asking
offer to find out with the class
questions.explanation: Finding out together shows that questions are welcome and models how to look for answers. Brushing the question aside kills curiosity.

questions.stem: In an EVS discussion, a child shares an idea that is wrong. The teacher should first
options: tell the child the idea is silly
write the right answer on the board
move on to another child at once
ask others what they think and why
questions.explanation: Asking the class to reason about the idea lets the child and others test it, which changes thinking more than simply being corrected.

questions.stem: Why do some EVS questions, such as 'How do people in your area travel?', have more than one right answer?
questions.explanation: EVS draws on each child's own surroundings, so answers differ from home to home and every honest answer is valid.

questions.stem: In Freud's theory, the part of personality that works on the pleasure principle is the
questions.explanation: The id seeks immediate pleasure. The ego works on the reality principle and the superego is the conscience.

questions.stem: The Rorschach inkblot test is an example of a
questions.explanation: In a projective test, a person reads meaning into an unclear picture and so reveals inner feelings. The Thematic Apperception Test is another projective test.

questions.stem: Which learning objective belongs to the affective domain?
options: Names the parts of a flowering plant
Shows interest in caring for plants
Measures the height of a seedling
Draws a neat diagram of a leaf
questions.explanation: The affective domain covers feelings, interests and values. Naming parts is cognitive, and drawing or measuring are mainly skills.

questions.stem: 'Emile', a book arguing that education should follow the child's own nature, was written by
questions.explanation: Jean-Jacques Rousseau's Emile (1762) argued that children learn best from nature and experience, an idea that shaped child-centred education.

questions.stem: Who founded the school at Shantiniketan, where children learnt in the open, close to nature?
questions.explanation: Tagore started his school at Shantiniketan in 1901 with classes under the trees; it later grew into Visva-Bharati.

questions.stem: A test that checks whether each child can do a stated skill, without comparing children, is
questions.explanation: A criterion-referenced test compares each child with a fixed standard. A norm-referenced test compares a child with other children.

questions.stem: A test that gives nearly the same scores when given again to the same children is
questions.explanation: Reliability is consistency of scores. Validity is whether the test measures what it claims to measure; a test can be reliable but not valid.

questions.stem: A Class 3 child with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) struggles through long lessons. Which step helps her most?
options: Punishment each time she gets up
Longer written work to calm her
A seat at the back, out of the way
questions.explanation: Children with ADHD learn better with work broken into short, clear tasks, regular chances to move and a seat near the teacher, away from distractions. Punishment and long tasks make focus harder.

questions.stem: सरिता ने मेले से क्या खरीदने का निश्चय किया?
questions.explanation: The passage says she decided to buy a book of stories, not toys.

questions.stem: सहेलियाँ अगले दिन किताबों की दुकान क्यों ढूँढ़ने लगीं?
questions.explanation: After hearing Sarita read a funny story, the same friends who had laughed went looking for books: the story made them want to read.

questions.stem: गद्यांश में आए "मज़ाक उड़ाना" का अर्थ क्या है?
questions.explanation: मज़ाक उड़ाना means to make fun of someone, which the friends did before they heard the story.

questions.stem: किस वाक्य में कोई व्याकरणिक अशुद्धि नहीं है?
options: मैंने यह काम कर लिया है।
मेरे को यह काम करना है।
मैं यह काम कर लिया है।
मैंने यह काम कर लिया हूँ।
questions.explanation: With a transitive verb in the perfect tense, the subject takes ने (मैंने) and the verb agrees with the object: कर लिया है. मेरे को is a common error for मुझे.

questions.stem: किस शब्द की वर्तनी शुद्ध है?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is परीक्षा: परि + ईक्षा gives a long ई, and the conjunct is क्ष, not क्श.

questions.stem: "बचपन" कौन-सी संज्ञा है?
questions.explanation: बचपन names a state or quality (from बच्चा), not a person, place or group, so it is a भाववाचक संज्ञा, like बुढ़ापा and मित्रता.

questions.stem: कक्षा 3 में नई कविता पढ़ाते समय पहला चरण क्या होना चाहिए?
questions.explanation: Children should first hear the poem read well, with rhythm and feeling, to enjoy it. Word meanings and questions come after.

questions.stem: कक्षा 2 में "शब्द-दीवार" (नए शब्दों को चित्रों सहित दीवार पर लगाना) का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या है?
questions.explanation: A word wall keeps new words in view, so children meet, read and use them again and again in their own writing.

questions.stem: कक्षा 5 में पत्र-लेखन सिखाने का सबसे अच्छा तरीका क्या है?
questions.explanation: Writing a real letter to a real person (a grandparent, the headteacher) gives a purpose and an audience, so the format is learnt in use.

questions.stem: कक्षा 1 में अक्षर लिखना सिखाने से पहले कौन-सी गतिविधि उपयोगी है?
questions.explanation: Drawing lines, curves and shapes builds hand control and eye-hand coordination, which children need before forming letters.

questions.stem: What did Leela do when the power failed?
options: She studied alone by a candle
She turned her revision into a quiz
She went to bed early that night
She asked a neighbour to fix the lights
questions.explanation: She lit the lantern, gathered her brothers and turned her revision into a quiz.

questions.stem: 'Leela did not panic' means that she
questions.explanation: To panic is to lose control through sudden fear. She did the opposite: she stayed calm and made a plan.

questions.stem: Who was 'begging for more questions'?
questions.explanation: 'The boys were begging for more questions' refers to her two younger brothers, who joined the quiz.

questions.stem: Choose the correct question tag: 'They have left already, ___?'
questions.explanation: A positive statement takes a negative tag with the same helping verb: have becomes haven't they.

questions.stem: 'To get cold feet' means to
options: lose courage at the last moment
walk too far in one day
questions.explanation: To get cold feet is to become nervous and back out just before doing something planned, as in 'He got cold feet before the speech.'

questions.stem: In 'She sings sweetly', the word 'sweetly' is
questions.explanation: 'Sweetly' tells how she sings, so it modifies the verb and is an adverb. 'Sweet' would be the adjective.

questions.stem: Using picture flashcards in a Class 1 English lesson mainly helps children
questions.explanation: A picture beside the word lets children connect the English word to its meaning without translation.

questions.stem: Drawing a mind map before writing a paragraph helps children to
questions.explanation: A mind map is a planning tool: ideas branch from a central topic, so writing has a clear order.

questions.stem: In an information-gap activity, pairs of children
options: share details only the other one has
copy the same text from the board
answer the teacher's questions one by one
questions.explanation: Each partner holds information the other needs, so they must ask and answer in English to complete the task.

questions.stem: Teaching Class 2 children to use a picture dictionary mainly builds
questions.explanation: Looking up words with picture support lets children find meanings on their own, a habit that grows into dictionary skills.

questions.stem: A jar holds 8 litres 500 millilitres of lassi. How many glasses of 250 millilitres can be filled from it? Type the number only.
A school orders 23 packets of pencils with 48 pencils in each packet. How many pencils is that? Type the number only.
What is the smallest prime number?
questions.explanation: A prime has exactly two factors, 1 and itself. 1 has only one factor, so it is not prime; 2 is the smallest prime and the only even one.

questions.stem: Which of these numbers is a multiple of 7?
How many centimetres are there in 7 m 8 cm?
questions.explanation: 1 m = 100 cm, so 7 m 8 cm = 700 + 8 = 708 cm. Writing 8 cm as 80 gives 780.

questions.stem: What is the value of 63 / 7 x 3?
questions.explanation: Division and multiplication are done from left to right: 63 / 7 = 9, then 9 x 3 = 27. Doing 7 x 3 first gives 63 / 21 = 3.

questions.stem: If 4 June is a Friday, what day of the week is 4 July?
questions.explanation: June has 30 days, so 4 July is 30 days after 4 June. 30 = 4 weeks + 2 days, and two days after Friday is Sunday.

questions.stem: What is the best order for introducing multiplication?
options: The symbol x first, then objects
Tables learned by heart first, then groups
Objects in groups, then drawings, then x
questions.explanation: Concrete objects, then pictures, then symbols: children see equal groups and arrays before they meet the symbol.

questions.stem: A child says a triangle turned upside down is 'not a triangle any more'. She needs
options: to copy the shape ten times
to see shapes in many positions
to learn the formula for area
questions.explanation: Children who see shapes only in one textbook position think orientation matters. Turning cut-out shapes and finding them around the room fixes the idea.

questions.stem: A child writes 25 + 18 = 313. What has gone wrong?
options: She wrote 13 in the ones place
questions.explanation: 5 + 8 = 13, but she wrote the whole 13 instead of writing 3 and carrying 1 ten, then wrote 2 + 1 = 3 in front. Bundles of tens and ones show why the ten is carried.

questions.stem: Peer tutoring helps in mathematics mainly because children
options: need no help from the teacher
explain ideas in each other's words
can copy each other's written answers
questions.explanation: A classmate's explanation is often closer to the learner's own way of thinking, and the tutor deepens her own understanding by explaining.

questions.stem: Chand Baori, one of India's deepest stepwells, is at Abhaneri in which district?
questions.explanation: Chand Baori at Abhaneri in Dausa district has thousands of narrow steps on three sides going down to the water.

questions.stem: The camel festival held every January is famous in which city?
questions.explanation: Bikaner's camel festival has camel races, dances and decorated camels. Bikaner is also home to a national camel research centre.

questions.stem: Most of the Thar Desert lies on which side of the Aravalli hills?
questions.explanation: The Aravallis run from south-west to north-east across Rajasthan; the sandy Thar lies to their west, and the wetter, more fertile land to their east.

questions.stem: Which of these is a major cause of air pollution in towns?
questions.explanation: Exhaust from cars, buses and motorcycles adds smoke and harmful gases to town air. Trees and bicycles help keep air clean.

questions.stem: When a soaked gram seed sprouts, which part comes out first and grows down into the root?
questions.explanation: The radicle, the tiny root of the embryo, comes out first and grows downward. The plumule becomes the shoot, the cotyledons store food and the seed coat protects the seed.

questions.stem: Which of these animals is a mammal?
questions.explanation: Whales breathe air with lungs and feed their young on milk, so they are mammals. Sharks are fish, penguins birds and tortoises reptiles.

questions.stem: Woollen clothes keep us warm because wool
options: traps air that holds in heat
lets cold air pass through quickly
questions.explanation: Air trapped between wool fibres is a poor conductor of heat, so body heat is not lost easily. Wool does not make heat itself.

questions.stem: Braille, a script of raised dots, is read by
questions.explanation: Braille lets people who are blind read by touch. People who cannot hear may use sign language.

questions.stem: A Class 3 teacher keeps a 'question box' where children drop questions about the world. This mainly
questions.explanation: A question box tells children that their questions matter and gives the teacher topics to explore with the class.

questions.stem: What should follow a class visit to a post office?
options: Copying a long note from the board
A written test the next morning
A discussion of what children saw
questions.explanation: Talking, drawing or writing about the visit helps children make sense of their observations and share questions.

questions.stem: A Class 5 class debates whether old trees should be cut to widen a road. This mainly develops
questions.explanation: Discussing a real dilemma builds reasoning, listening to others and concern for the environment.

questions.stem: Children record the weather each day for a month on a class chart. This mainly develops
questions.explanation: Daily recording builds observation and lets children notice patterns, such as hotter afternoons or rainy weeks.
